Lady Harcourt’s remark fell into the conversation like a stone into a pond, and the ripples spread in every direction. Nobody laughed. Miss Vane lowered her eyes to her plate, where a small pile of peas had suddenly become fascinating, and the gentleman beside her coughed into his napkin. “How very original,” said Mrs. Brandt at last, in a tone that left no doubt that she meant the opposite. The footman moved around the table with the wine; the candles trembled. It was a long evening, and no one was sorry when the ladies rose to withdraw. In the hall, Miss Vane caught her reflection in a mirror and was surprised to find she looked perfectly calm.
